Berrien County issues construction and road updates for week of Oct. 5, 2026
Berrien County has announced updated schedules for road construction projects during the week of October 5, including bridge restrictions and detours across multiple townships. Several paving operations depend on weather conditions while some roads remain closed or under repair.
The Berrien County Road Department released an update on Oct. 5 regarding ongoing and upcoming road construction and maintenance activities throughout the county.
Countywide work includes pothole patching, shoulder maintenance, roadside mowing, bridge inspections, and annual road painting that began in July. New bridge weight restrictions have taken effect at several locations across the county.
In Benton Township, a temporary traffic signal is operating at Pipestone Road and Mall Drive due to infrastructure damage until repairs can be completed later this year. Yore Avenue construction between Napier Avenue and Townline Road has finished paving; contractors are working on shoulders, restoration, and pavement application as weather permits. More information or detour maps are available on the Berrien County website.
Bertrand Township reports Buffalo Road is open to traffic but final project work continues. The Dayton Road Bridge over Nat Rail Pass Co Amtrak now has new weight limits of 29 tons/37 tons/43 tons for different vehicle types. Red Bud Trail will be resurfaced in 2026, with final cleanup underway by contractors.
Other projects include new bridge weight restrictions for Minnich Road Bridge and Three Oaks Road Bridge in Chikaming Township; Paw Paw Lake Road Bridge in Coloma Township; Holden Road Bridge in Lincoln Township; Hochberger Road Bridge in Pipestone Township; as well as scheduled closures or detours such as Hennesey Road between Dan Smith and Angling Roads starting Sept. 1 for permit-related work expected to last three to four weeks.
Several subdivisions—including Hickory Creek Subdivision and Vineland Heights Subdivision—are scheduled for hot mix asphalt resurfacing from Oct. 6 through Oct. 8, dependent on weather conditions. Glendora Road Bridge remains closed with completion anticipated by Oct. 30, while Warren Woods Road will close temporarily for culvert work beginning Oct. 6.
The department noted that these updates do not represent a comprehensive list of all ongoing roadwork activities within Berrien County.
